e9e8887e6c Redesign Check print as a report beside OrcaSlicer's preview
# Check print live test, 2026-10-22

Untracked working note. Do not commit.

Build: `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app` from `claude/check-print-report-82ed92` at e9e8887e6c, copied to the scratchpad and re-signed as bundle id `io.jusprin.check-print-test`, launched with its own `--datadir` (a copy of Kenneth's config with the API keys blanked, agent off, `single_instance` false). Project: `~/Downloads/arrow_headband.3mf` (its embedded printer is Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle, not the A1 Kenneth used; nothing below depends on the printer). Later states added plates and objects through the instance's own MCP endpoint (`tests/mcp/probe.py`).

Evidence directory: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/462562e7-6c9f-4674-844d-00d14db091f3/scratchpad/evidence/` (window screenshots, referenced below as `evidence/NN-*.jpg`). Harness bitmaps: `.../scratchpad/harness-capture/` (run log `.../scratchpad/harness-cp.log`, `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`; the run deleted its own data dir).

How the app was driven, since it matters for what was and was not tested: the screen-control route was refused (both the background `app_click` and the display-scope `computer_batch` were aborted, and the fork's controls expose no AX actions), so the app was driven by key events posted to its pid (Cmd+R, Return/Home/Down/Up/Escape/C) and by `lldb` calls into the live process to focus a control or toggle the Legend switch the way a click would (`CheckToggle::toggle()` fires the same wxEVT_CHECKBOX). Screenshots came from the background `app_screenshot` tool, which works without taking over the screen. Posted mouse events never reach the app, so anything that needs a pointer (dragging a slider, wheel over the slider, hover states, clicking rows or the close button) is listed under "not tested" at the end. No source file was changed, nothing was built, nothing committed.

## Kenneth's findings 1–7

### 1. Blank white rounded pill at the top-left of the preview canvas — reproduced, identified
Steps: slice, open Check print. Observed on every opening (`evidence/01-dialog-initial-state.jpg`, `09-c-key-hides-gcode-listing.jpg`, harness `check-print-canvas-default.png`).
It is OrcaSlicer's plate-selector strip (`GLCanvas3D::_render_imgui_select_plate_toolbar`, called from `_render_overlays` at `src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp:8431`). `Preview::init` enables it for every editor preview (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_Preview.cpp:276`, `enable_select_plate_toolbar(true)`), and `Plater::create_preview` (Plater.cpp:17253) builds the dialog's preview through the same constructor. Why it is blank: hypothesis — the thumbnail textures are generated for the Plater's own preview canvas, never for this second canvas, so the item draws its frame with no image. Hidden by `set_legacy_overlays_hidden(true)` (GLCanvas3D.cpp:2151 skips `_render_overlays`).

### 2. 3D navigator cube at the bottom-left — reproduced
`_render_3d_navigator()` at GLCanvas3D.cpp:8463, inside `_render_overlays`. Same evidence as 1. Hidden by the same flag.

### 3. Canvas toolbar (menu and magnifier buttons) at the bottom-left — reproduced
`_render_canvas_toolbar()` at GLCanvas3D.cpp:8465, inside `_render_overlays`. Same evidence. Hidden by the same flag.

### 4. "Assemble-view" layers icon at the bottom-right — reproduced, but it is not the assemble toolbar
`Preview::init` disables the assemble toolbar (`GUI_Preview.cpp:280`, `enable_assemble_view_toolbar(false)`). The icon is the layer slider's own "show one layer" button: `IMSlider::render` draws it at the canvas's bottom-right corner (`src/slic3r/GUI/IMSlider.cpp:1273-1285`, `ImGui::ImageButton3(normal_id, hover_id, ONE_LAYER_BUTTON_SIZE)`), from textures loaded at IMSlider.cpp:155-162: `resources/images/one_layer_off.svg` (fills `#009688` teal and `#fff`), plus `one_layer_on`, `_hover` and `_dark` variants. It is drawn from `GCodeViewer::render_slider`, not from `_render_overlays`, so hiding the legacy overlays keeps it, which is what Kenneth wants.
Brand colour at no upstream cost: partly. The fork's resource overlay (`resources/jusprin/overlay/images`, installed by `BrandPalette.cpp:124`) hooks `Slic3r::var()`, but IMSlider builds the path from `Slic3r::resources_dir() + "/images/..."` directly (IMSlider.cpp:155), so an overlay SVG would not apply. Either edit the eight SVGs in `resources/images` in place (resource files, no code) or change those eight lines to `var(...)`.
Evidence: `evidence/01`, `09`, harness `check-print-canvas-default.png` (green stack bottom-right).

### 5. "Untitled" and "01" on the bed — reproduced; hiding legacy overlays would not remove the number
Visible once the camera shows the plate (`evidence/06-finding-selected-marker-box-shown.jpg`, `09`, `20`). The plate number is drawn by `PartPlate::render_only_numbers(bottom)` at `src/slic3r/GUI/PartPlate.cpp:3394-3397`, which runs whether or not `only_body` is set (the flag the legacy-overlay switch turns on, GLCanvas3D.cpp:2062). The name texture goes through `render_icons(bottom, only_body, hover_id)` (PartPlate.cpp:3394); whether `only_body` suppresses it there is unverified. Note that Prepare's canvas, which has the controller attached, shows both labels too (`evidence/00a-prepare-canvas-before-slicing-shows-plate-name-and-number.jpg`), so this is not a difference between the two canvases.

Verification of the hypothesis for 1–5: `PreviewPresentationController` (CanvasPresentationController.cpp:84-103) never calls `set_legacy_overlays_hidden`; `CanvasPresentationController::attach` does (line 22-23) and Prepare attaches it at ShellController.cpp:609. So 1, 2 and 3 are explained by that one missing call; 5 is not (see above); 4 is unaffected by it.

### 6. OrcaSlicer's G-code listing is drawn over the bed and the Legend switch does not hide it — reproduced exactly
Steps: open the window (listing present, `evidence/01-dialog-initial-state.jpg`); Legend on (listing stays, moves down below the legend, `02-dialog-legend-on.jpg`); Legend off (listing back where it was, `03-dialog-legend-off-again.jpg`).
Verified in code: the listing is `GCodeViewer::SequentialView::GCodeWindow::render`, called from `SequentialView::render` whenever a path exists (GCodeViewer.cpp:972), with no legend condition; its own gate is `wxGetApp().show_gcode_window()` (GCodeViewer.cpp:810), which is `GUI_App::m_show_gcode_window{true}` (GUI_App.hpp:337) read from the app config key `show_gcode_window` (GUI_App.cpp:910). It is not inside `_render_overlays`, so the legacy flag would not touch it either. Proof: pressing C (GLCanvas3D.cpp:3549 → `toggle_show_gcode_window`) with the canvas focused removed it (`evidence/09-c-key-hides-gcode-listing.jpg`). The legend's `</>` button calls the same toggle (GCodeViewer.cpp:3470); not pressed (needs the mouse). The View menu's "Show G-code Window" item is disabled while the modal is open.
Side effect, see 16: C persists the change to the user's app config.

### 7. Tool-position box at the bottom centre, over the moves slider, also with Legend off — reproduced
Steps: open, select the first finding (layer slider goes to layer 1), box appears "X 5.390 Y 249.130 Z 0.200 / Speed: 105 Bottom surface" over the left end of the moves slider (`evidence/06-finding-selected-marker-box-shown.jpg`); Legend on (`07`), Legend off (`08-legend-off-marker-box-still-shown.jpg`): the box stays.
Verified in code: `SequentialView::render` draws `marker.render_position_window` when `m_show_marker` (GCodeViewer.cpp:959), positioned at 0.5·width, bottom edge (GCodeViewer.cpp:335). `m_show_marker` is set in `GCodeViewer::render` at line 1596 when the visible range's end differs from the full range's end, and it is sticky until the next `load_toolpaths` (line 1388). So it appears when the moves slider is anywhere but the end, and also after `show_finding` moves the layer slider down (the layer change shortens the range). One quirk seen: after a keyboard move of the slider the box only appears on the next frame, because line 1596 is evaluated before `render_slider` applies the slider at line 1639 (`evidence/04`, `05` show the moved slider with no box; lldb read `m_show_marker=false` with visible range end 347340 vs full 347343; the box came with the next frame).

## New findings

### 8. Keyboard focus is trapped in the preview canvas: Tab never reaches Legend, Close or the report
Steps: open the window; press Tab (any number of times). `wxWindow::FindFocus()` read in lldb stays on the `GLCanvas` after Tab; with the report panel focused it stays on `Print report` after three Tabs. Only Escape works from the keyboard.
Verified: the canvas turns Tab into `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` (GLCanvas3D.cpp:3747-3750), which only the Plater's own canvases bind (Plater.cpp:5185 and 5255); the dialog's preview has no handler, so Tab is swallowed. The report panel is created with `wxWANTS_CHARS` (CheckPrintReportPanel.cpp:133), which on macOS also keeps Tab from traversing. Expected: Tab order canvas → Legend → Close → report (design-system keyboard rules); the focus ring code exists on CheckToggle and the Quiet button but can never be reached.

### 9. Selecting a row from the keyboard does not scroll it into view
Steps: a report taller than the panel (22 first-layer rows, content 1302 px in a 911 px panel); focus the panel; press Up (selects the last row). Observed: `m_selected = {0,21}`, `m_scroll = 0`, caption and camera update, but the highlighted row is below the fold (`evidence/16-keyboard-selected-last-row-not-scrolled-into-view.jpg`; after setting `m_scroll` to the bottom it is there, `17-long-report-scrolled-to-bottom.jpg`). Verified: `CheckPrintReportPanel::select` (CheckPrintReportPanel.cpp:~170) and `on_key` never adjust `m_scroll`.

### 10. A long report gives no sign that it scrolls
Same state as 9: rows run off the bottom edge with no scrollbar, fade or cut row (`evidence/15-long-report-22-rows-no-scroll-indicator.jpg`). The wheel scrolls it (code; not driven here). The boards do not show the overflow case, so this may be a design gap rather than a code bug.

### 11. The finding caption sits on top of OrcaSlicer's overlays
With Legend off the caption is drawn over the G-code listing's first lines (`evidence/06`); with Legend on it covers the legend's view-type dropdown row (`evidence/07-legend-on-with-marker-caption-overlaps-legend.jpg`). `draw_caption` places it at canvas width − 76 DIP, top = space_3 (CheckPrintDialog.cpp, `kCaptionRightInsetDip`), which is the corner the legend and G-code window occupy, and it calls `BringWindowToDisplayFront` so it always wins. The board (`check-print-03`) assumes that corner is empty. Goes away for the listing once 6 is fixed; the legend-on overlap remains.

### 12. The window opens with whatever camera Prepare had, not fitted to the plate
Steps: zoom Prepare in (any way; here OrcaSlicer's preview had been zoomed by Cmd+R), open Check print. Observed: the first opening showed a corner of the headband (`evidence/01`), the second plate opened as a solid red wall (`12-second-plate-opens-with-prepare-camera-zoomed-in.jpg`), the cubes plate opened on empty grey (`15`). Verified: the constructor sets up the preview and report but never calls `zoom_to_gcode`/`zoom_to_bed`; the camera is the Plater's shared one (`m_plater.get_camera()`), and only `show_finding` moves it. Board `check-print-01` shows the whole plate on opening. Closing does put Prepare's camera back (checked after a finding moved it, `evidence/00`-style main-window screenshot matched the pre-open view).

### 13. No minimum window size; at 900×600 OrcaSlicer's overlays pile on each other
`GetMinSize()` is (−1,−1) and the dialog has `wxRESIZE_BORDER`. At 900×600 the panel keeps 360 and the preview is 540 wide: the moves slider's left end sits under the magnifier button and the navigator overlaps the listing (`evidence/13-window-900x600-overlays-collide.jpg`). At 1700×1050 the layout is fine (`14-window-1700x1050.jpg`); the panel width stays, nothing clipped.

### 14. Dark mode: the Close button draws a lighter box behind the X
Steps: dark mode (set per app with `defaults write io.jusprin.check-print-test AppleInterfaceStyle Dark`; `mac_dark_mode()` reads that key, MacDarkMode.mm:28), open Check print. Observed: a grey square behind the X at the header's right (`evidence/19-dark-mode-dialog-crossing-paths-case.jpg`, `20`); in light mode nothing. Verified: `HeaderButton::draw` clears and fills a `HeaderStyle::Quiet` button with `surface_canvas` (HeaderControls.cpp:~406 and the `fill` expression that follows), while `build_header` paints the header `surface_raised` (CheckPrintDialog.cpp); the two tokens coincide in light and differ in dark. Everything else in dark reads correctly: panel, summary, pink (action) sliders, value boxes with pink text on dark, caption.

### 15. A stale hover tooltip ("40m22s") and hover ring sit on the layer slider with no pointer in the window
Seen at the top of the layer slider from the first frame, and it stayed there after the handle moved to the bottom (`evidence/02`, `03`, `04`, `06`). lldb: `ImGui::GetIO().MousePos = (823,102)` with `DisplaySize = (835,911)` while the real pointer was on another display. Hypothesis: the single ImGui context keeps the last mouse position fed by another canvas (commit 570a723ad0 gives each canvas its own size per frame, not its own mouse state), so the dialog's slider sees a hover at a point it never received a mouse-move for and draws the layer-time tooltip (IMSlider.cpp:873-874).

### 16. Pressing C inside Check print changes and persists the app-wide "Show G-code Window" preference
Steps: canvas focused, press C. Observed: listing hidden, and `datadir/JusPrin2.conf` now has `"show_gcode_window": false` (checked with grep; pressing C again set it back to true). Verified: GLCanvas3D.cpp:3549 → `GUI_App::toggle_show_gcode_window` writes `app_config->set_bool` (GUI_App.cpp:716-719). A modal review window silently edits a global preference; the same is true of the legend's `</>` button.

### 17. The panel follows the active plate; the header shows the stale-close path works from outside the app
Not bugs, recorded as verified behaviour: with three plates the window opened on the active one each time ("Second plate · towel-box-bottom.stl …", `evidence/12`; "Cubes · towel-box-spring.stl and 21 more …", `15`; "Plate 1 · arrow headband.STL and 1 more …", `19`). A process setting changed through the MCP endpoint while the window was open closed it within 2 s. Escape closes from the canvas and from the panel. The summary matched OrcaSlicer's legend totals (legend 40m22s / 5.74 m / 18.22 g / 0.46 against panel 40 min / 5.7 m / 18 g / $0.46; `slice_report` printTimeSeconds 2422). Section order held in every case seen: harness cp_b Supports first (`harness-capture/check-print-supports.png`), cp_c OrcaSlicer warnings (red) → Unsupported islands (amber) → First layer (`check-print-island.png`), live Crossing paths (red) → First layer (`19`); each closing line named exactly the checks not shown. Five openings across two instances with re-slices and plate changes in between: no crash, no assertion; the only `[error]` lines in `datadir/log/debug_*.log` are OrcaSlicer's own (`call_process:got cancelled exception` from cancelled slices, `gcode path conflicts found`).

## Deviations from the boards (not filed as bugs)
- Boards 01/02 have a second header checkbox, "Moves slider", off at opening; the build has only Legend and always shows the moves slider (the commit message says this was deliberate; the brief says Kenneth is undecided).
- The caption title is drawn in ImGui's regular font; board 03 uses `label-bold` for the title and `label` for "Layer N · Z mm".
- The Supports section count reads "43 layers"; the board writes "2 objects · 96 layers".

## Side observations outside Check print (lower confidence, from the route used)
- Cmd+R (OrcaSlicer's slice accelerator) switches the main window to OrcaSlicer's Preview tab with its legend, listing and toolbars (`evidence/00-main-window-after-cmd-r-slice.jpg`, `18`). Probably pre-existing; not checked against `jusprin-newui`.
- The print-actions popup stayed open with stale rows while the slice finished underneath ("Slice all plates" as the only row while the primary button already read "Print plate 2", `evidence/11-two-plates-menu-lacks-check-print.jpg`); a posted Escape did not close it. My keys are posted to the pid rather than typed, so treat this as a lead, not a repro.

## Not reproduced / not tested, and why
- Mouse-driven checks: dragging either slider, wheel over the layer slider, hover highlight on rows, clicking a row or a section header, the Close button, the legend's `</>` and collapse buttons. No pointer route (see the top). Keyboard and lldb equivalents were used instead; the harness covers `panel.select`, `toggle_section` and the switch.
- Two filaments: the project has one filament slot, `printer_setup_preview` refused a second preset ("This project has 1 filament slots"), and there is no keyboard route to add a slot. The harness has no two-filament case either. The per-extruder rows and the "Changes" row in `draw_summary` are untested.
- Supports section live: only the harness (cp_b PASS, bitmap above); no live opening with generated supports.
- Undo/redo keys while the window is modal: not tried.
- Opening on a small main window: the dialog takes the plater's client size at opening; I resized the dialog itself instead (13).
- Wrapping and ellipsis of long object names: the harness caption shows the ellipsis ("20mmbox-LF.stl · 400 mm² o…", `check-print-canvas-default.png`) and the panel wrapped the crossing-paths message over two lines (`19`); no object name long enough to ellipsize in a row was available.

lines: `GLCanvas3D` keeps a small API for controlling how its parts are presented. That API contains nothing specific to JusPrin. A controller in fork-owned code uses the API to apply JusPrin's choices, and puts OrcaSlicer's previous state back when the controller is destroyed. Whether a control is drawn and whether it receives input must be two separate switches. Otherwise a control that is hidden could still swallow pointer events. OrcaSlicer's native gizmos (the on-canvas tools such as Move and Rotate) must stay usable while one is active.

-The Check print window's preview has its own controller, `PreviewPresentationController` beside `CanvasPresentationController`: it switches OrcaSlicer's legend through `GCodeViewer::show_legend` and restores it when destroyed. Both sliders stay as OrcaSlicer draws them.

+The Check print window's preview has its own controller, `PreviewPresentationController` beside `CanvasPresentationController`. It hides the canvas's legacy overlay layer (plate selector strip, 3D navigator, canvas toolbar), holds OrcaSlicer's app-wide G-code listing preference (`show_gcode_window`) off while the window is open, and switches the legend through `GCodeViewer::show_legend`; destroying it restores all three, on every close path. Both sliders stay as OrcaSlicer draws them. OrcaSlicer's single ImGui context also keeps the last pointer position of whichever canvas saw it, so the window clears it when it opens and when the pointer leaves its canvas.

The POC had one broad switch, `render_overlays`. Production needs finer control. Treat each of these as its own item that can be shown or hidden separately: OrcaSlicer's main toolbar, the gizmo picker, the handles of the active gizmo, plate actions, object labels, layer-editing controls, navigation aids, the Preview legend, and the Preview sliders. Some controls are shared between canvases, such as `Plater`'s collapse toolbar. A shared control must be saved and restored by one object that lives as long as the shell does. Do not give each canvas its own guard for it.

I've fixed everything from the live-test report in fork code and committed it on `claude/check-print-report-82ed92` as two new commits, 53471f582b and 713f02b03c, on top of e9e8887e6c. I added them as new commits rather than squashing, so no history was rewritten and no approval was needed. Nothing is pushed.

The upstream footprint is unchanged: the 16 lines in `Color.hpp`, the ImGuiWrapper files, `IMSlider.cpp` and `GLCanvas3D.cpp`. No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed in this round. I haven't rechecked the fixes in the live app yet.

**What changed, by report item**
- **1–3, plate strip, navigator cube, canvas toolbar:** the window hides OrcaSlicer's legacy overlay layer on open and restores it on close, as Prepare does.
- **6 and 16, G-code listing:** the window remembers the app-wide "show G-code window" setting, turns it off on open, and restores it on every close path, which also undoes a C key pressed inside. Turning it on inside the window is left alone until close.
- **8, keyboard focus:** Tab and Shift+Tab now move through canvas, report, Legend and Close, and around. This includes the canvas's own Tab event. Escape closes from any of them.
- **9 and 10, scrolling:** a row selected from the keyboard scrolls into view. A report taller than its panel shows a thin scrollbar: surface-subtle track, border-strong thumb, radius-small. Its width and inset reuse the 4 DIP spacing token, because there is no scrollbar token yet.
- **11, caption:** it sits top-left at the space-3 inset, with the title in the bold font. In a narrow preview it now ends with an ellipsis before OrcaSlicer's legend; the legend reached into that corner in the pictures.
- **12, camera:** the window opens fitted to the slice, and Prepare's own view comes back on close.
- **13, minimum size:** the window can't shrink below 900 × 600 DIP. At that size the sliders, their value boxes and the panel stay apart.
- **14, dark Close button:** header buttons can now take the surface they sit on. Only the Close button uses this; every other button keeps its old surface.
- **15, stale hover:** the window clears ImGui's pointer position when it opens, when the pointer leaves its canvas, and on close. No upstream line was needed.
- **Supports count:** it now reads "1 object · 43 layers", from a new objects count in the fork's support check.

**What the tests prove**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full build | passes |
| Catch2 report-model tests | 63 assertions pass, including the new scroll and scrollbar arithmetic |
| Agent suite | 15,114 assertions pass |
| `--check-print` harness, light | 169 checks pass |
| `--check-print` harness, dark | passes |
| Default, `--print-issues`, `--print-issue-readers` runs | 566, 484 and 253 checks pass |

With the fixes temporarily undone, the matching harness checks failed, nine in all, including overlays, listing, hover, camera fit, minimum size, the dark Close button, scrollbar and scroll-into-view. I looked at the canvas pictures for default, Legend on, selected finding and minimum size, in light and dark, and at the panel pictures.

**Limits**
- **Focus depends on the app being in front.** macOS only gives keyboard focus to the frontmost app. Real Tab movement was observed and passed in four runs, and logged as unobserved in the others. The Tab order itself is checked every run.
- **Pointer-only behaviour is untested:** wheel scrolling, dragging, hover, clicking rows or Close, and pointer-leave clearing the hover. The harness checks the reset when the window opens, starting from a simulated stale pointer.

The brief, logs, build scripts and pictures are untracked in the worktree root. The light pictures are in `check-print-capture/` and the dark ones in `check-print-capture-dark/`.
